Subject: Private/VPC data flow review - Acme / next steps

Hi Jane / Acme security team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet everyone. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on data handling and the Private/VPC options we discussed.

Recap from our call (high level):
- Primary concern: PII in prompts/inputs and inference outputs; need to ensure no customer-identifiable data leaves Acme-controlled network.
- Retention: Acme policy = short-term request-level retention (90 days) for troubleshooting; audit logs retained for 12 months.
- Logging/observability: Need control over debug-level logs, ability to redact tokens containing PII, and exportable audit logs for compliance audits.
- Data residency: All inference compute must stay in customer VPC or on-prem; no routing through public hosted control plane that stores request payloads.
- Deployment preference: Private (customer VPC) or on-prem (air-gapped) if we can meet procurement and operational constraints.

Technical notes from Redwood side (summary):
- Redwood Private can be deployed with a customer-controlled VPC and private control plane; model assets and inference stay inside the VPC.
- We support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest; network egress can be restricted to only KMS endpoints or internal registries.
- Optional on-prem/air-gapped mode is supported: model sync via signed artifacts and an offline installer.

Ask / next steps from Acme:
1) Could you share your network diagram (internet egress points, NATs, firewalls, and FQDN allowlist policy)?
2) Confirm the exact list of PII types we must treat as sensitive (SSNs, emails, phone numbers, device IDs, etc.).
3) Please point to the procurement contact for a follow-up on licensing and NDA.

I've attached our Private/VPC overview for reference. Rishi (cc) — can you add any technical clarifications if I missed anything?

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers and clarifications below.

PII scope:
- Confirmed: Names, emails, phone numbers, SSNs, payment tokens, device identifiers, and any customer-provided PII in prompts must be protected.
- We treat hashed identifiers as PII for our policies unless explicitly proven irreversible.

Retention:
- Request payloads: 90 days max (for debugging and minimal logging)
- Audit logs / access logs: 12 months (must be exportable in CSV/JSON for auditors)

Logging controls / redaction:
- We need the ability to redact tokens containing PII before logs are stored off-host.
- Debug traces containing full prompt+response must be opt-in and retained only in our environment.

Data residency / deployment:
- Priority: Private VPC deployment with no egress of request payloads to public internet.
- If Private VPC isn't possible for some components (control plane), it must be limited to metadata only and not store request payloads.
- On-prem air-gap is preferred for certain regulated workloads; what are the constraints for model updates?

Attached is our security questionnaire excerpt and our high-level network boundary diagram (redacted).

Procurement contact: procurement@acme-corp.com

If you can provide a proposed network diagram from Redwood for the Private deployment and a short note on egress/KMS behavior we can review with our infra team.

Best,

Jane Park

Jane — thanks for the detail. Quick technical responses and a proposed deployment pattern.

Proposed Private/VPC pattern (high level):
- Control plane: two options
  1) Private control plane within Acme VPC (preferred): Redwood control plane components run in customer subnets; lifecycle APIs talk to management endpoints over private networking. No request payloads leave the VPC.
  2) Hosted control plane with metadata-only APIs over PrivateLink: control plane accepts metadata/state but all request/response payloads are kept on customer-hosted inference nodes. We do not persist request payloads in the hosted control plane.

- Inference nodes: run in customer VPC (ECS/GKE/AKS or on-prem VMs). Model weights stored on customer-managed storage encrypted with customer KMS keys.

- Egress controls:
  - Outbound traffic can be restricted to customer-approved endpoints only (KMS endpoints, private image registries, or specific AWS S3 endpoints).
  - We support routing model update downloads through a signed artifact repository accessible over private endpoints or via an offline signed bundle for air-gapped installs.

- Logging / redaction:
  - Token-level redaction hooks can be configured to drop or hash tokens matching PII regexes before logs are written.
  - Audit logs are buffered locally and can be exported to your Splunk/Datadog or S3 bucket under your control.

- On-prem/air-gapped constraints and model updates:
  - We provide an offline model bundle process: Redwood packages model artifacts, signs them, and provides a secure transfer mechanism (customer-managed media or signed S3 export) for import into your air-gapped environment.
  - Upgrades are scheduled with a pre-tested compatibility matrix and an offline verification step; this adds operational lead time (typically 2–4 weeks per major model update depending on validation requirements).

Next steps (technical):
1) Acme to share network diagram and allowlist requirements (we need NAT/GW details and CIDR blocks).
2) We will produce a Redwood Private reference architecture diagram tailored to Acme's VPC.
3) Exchange a short statement of work (SOW) and a security addendum / data processing agreement for legal to review.

I've attached a draft network diagram showing the placement of control plane & inference nodes in-customer VPC (redacted example). Happy to walk the infra team through it next week.

—Rishi
